edits.html:
Hears Voices or Holds Odd Beliefs

primary psychosis · psychosis inside mood episodes · personality traits · normal and developmental · trauma, drugs and illnessPersistent psychosis, or mood, a drug, an illness, a trauma disorder or a lifelong trait?

ComparisonPractice
Bottom line

First rule out a drug or a medical illness, including delirium; a trauma disorder alone does not typically explain psychosis.

Then sort with three questions:

  • Persistent psychosis? Personality disorders may have odd perceptions or stress voices that pass within hours (under 24 hours); primary psychotic disorders have delusions or voices that persist
  • Only inside mood episodes? Then it is a mood disorder with psychotic features; Criterion A with a major mood episode, plus delusions or hallucinations 2 weeks or more without one, and mood episodes most of the illness, is schizoaffective
  • How long? 1 day to under 1 month, brief psychotic; 1 to under 6 months, schizophreniform; 6 months or more with a fall in function, schizophrenia

One or more delusions for 1 month or more, without prominent voices or disorganization, is delusional disorder.

Comparison
Practice
  1. 15-year-old girl, 7 months of talking to "Mira," a girl only she can hear sure her classmates are plotting against her grades fell; quit soccer; stays in her room; normal early development urine toxicology negative · T 36.8 °C → Schizophrenia → a voice and a persecutory belief for over 6 months with a fall in function in a teenager: schizophrenia; a normal imaginary companion comes without withdrawal or decline, and autism dates from the early developmental period and has no hallucinations
  2. 26-year-old man, since his teens believes he can sense others' thoughts wears odd, mismatched outfits; speaks in vague, odd phrases few close friends; works steadily as a night clerk no hallucinations or fixed delusions · BP 120/78 mm Hg → Schizotypal personality disorder → lifelong magical thinking, eccentric dress and speech and few relationships, short of frank psychosis: schizotypal; paranoid personality has distrust without odd beliefs, and schizophrenia needs persistent psychosis with a fall in function
  3. 48-year-old man, distrustful of coworkers since early adulthood suspects they exploit him; reads threats into harmless remarks no odd beliefs or eccentric habits; no voices no fixed false belief despite evidence · BP 128/80 mm Hg → Paranoid personality disorder → lifelong suspicion and hypervigilance with no persistent delusion or hallucination: paranoid personality disorder; delusional disorder needs one or more delusions for a month or more, and schizotypal adds odd beliefs and eccentricity
  4. 34-year-old man, always prefers solitary work and has no close friends indifferent to praise; shows little emotion no odd beliefs or eccentric behavior; normal early development no voices or delusions · BP 118/76 mm Hg → Schizoid personality disorder → a lifelong preference for being alone with detachment and little emotion, without odd beliefs: schizoid; schizotypal adds odd beliefs and eccentricity, and autism starts in the early developmental period with restricted, repetitive behaviors
  5. 24-year-old man, 9 months of believing he is a hidden prince speech jumps between unrelated topics; stopped working mood even; sleeps 8 hours a night; no drug use urine toxicology negative · T 36.7 °C → Schizophrenia → a grandiose delusion with disorganized speech for over 6 months and a fall in function: schizophrenia; in bipolar disorder the psychosis sits inside a mood episode, and delusional disorder has no prominent disorganization
  6. 23-year-old woman heard a voice calling her worthless for 3 hours after a breakup years of stormy relationships, mood swings and cutting back to her usual self by evening no drug use · HR 84/min → Borderline personality disorder → a voice under stress lasting hours, on a background of unstable relationships, mood and self-harm: borderline personality disorder; brief psychotic disorder needs at least 1 day, and schizophreniform at least 1 month
Pairs with Psychosis: timing and treatment of each psychotic disorder. Bipolar Disorder: is there a manic episode? Psychiatric Symptoms from Medical Illness or Medication: did a drug or disease start it?
Transferable rule

After ruling out a drug or a medical illness, decide whether the psychosis persists, whether it lives only inside mood episodes, and how long it has lasted.
